summary: The main risks are not the overall direction but boundary contracts: launcher import cost, cross-platform path resolution, portable host configuration, storage migration safety, and packaging completeness. Existing code provides useful primitives, but several are intentionally POSIX- or repository-scoped and cannot be reused unchanged for the proposed global runtime.

suggestions.title: Keep the launcher import boundary genuinely stdlib-only
suggestions.rationale: The three console scripts currently enter different stacks: `parrot` imports Click, `bookstore` imports Click and configuration at module load, while `wikitoolkit` has a deliberately `sys`-only dispatcher for the hook fast path. Make the launcher dispatch from `argv[0]`, decide re-exec before importing any target, and preserve the existing `wikitoolkit claude-hook` fast path after re-exec.

suggestions.title: Extract PARROT_HOME resolution into a dependency-free common module
suggestions.rationale: `parrot_home()` is duplicated because importing `wiki.project` drags in Pydantic and the wiki graph, while `bookstore.config` explicitly avoids that chain. Consolidating through `project.py` would violate the launcher and hook constraints; extract the environment/path primitive into a stdlib-only module and have the existing callers delegate to it.

suggestions.title: Specify venv resolution as a subprocess-tested state machine
suggestions.rationale: The proposed precedence crosses managed, project, linked-worktree, `PARROT_VENV`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and fallback cases. Existing worktree parsing handles `gitdir`, `commondir`, and `pyvenv.cfg`, but it does not provide the launcher contract. Add tests that invoke each console script from managed and project environments, cover missing requested scripts, linked worktrees, symlinked interpreters, Windows `Scripts`/`.exe` names, `--project`, and no-candidate fallback.

suggestions.title: Centralize only low-level cross-platform binary resolution
suggestions.rationale: Claude, Codex, and Google each independently hardcode `<root>/.venv/bin/<name>`, and Google’s managed-entry detection uses `PurePosixPath`, which will not recognize a Windows path reliably. Keep the host adapters separate as required, but share a small stdlib resolver that handles `bin` versus `Scripts`, `.exe`, absolute paths, and bare-command fallback.

suggestions.title: Define portable configuration as a complete ownership and cwd contract
suggestions.rationale: A bare command alone does not remove all machine-specific state: Google entries currently retain absolute `cwd`, toolkit entries retain absolute `--config`, and bookstore entries retain absolute `cwd` plus `sys.executable`. Claude reconciliation also unconditionally replaces the `wikitoolkit` entry, so a later default install can undo `--portable`. Specify which fields are omitted or made runtime-relative per host, and test explicit transitions between default and portable modes.

suggestions.title: Separate install requirements from import probes and post-install behavior
suggestions.rationale: `requires_dist` currently contains import names and availability is checked with `find_spec`; that cannot reliably represent PyPI distribution names or version constraints. Add a distinct PEP 508 package field and make post-install actions declarative, versioned handler identifiers rather than arbitrary template commands. Otherwise `self add` will either install the wrong thing or execute unreviewed package metadata.

suggestions.title: Make migration safety a storage-layer protocol, not a launcher feature
suggestions.rationale: SQLite migration is currently guarded by an asyncio lock scoped to one `SQLiteWikiStore` instance, while the existing filesystem lock is POSIX-only and becomes a no-op on Windows. Foreign stores are deliberately read-only and never migrate. Implement backup, cross-process locking, migration transactionality, and the minimum-runtime stamp where stores are opened, with older runtimes failing before writes or incompatible reads.

suggestions.title: Treat SDD asset packaging as a verified build artifact
suggestions.rationale: The current wheel metadata packages selected `_subagent_data`, `_rules_data`, and toolkit templates, but nothing packages `.claude` or `sdd/templates`; `MANIFEST.in` only covers Cython sources. Add a deterministic source-to-package sync step, include the complete asset set in the wheel, and enforce CI byte equality plus wheel-content checks. Do not make runtime installation depend on the monorepo checkout.

suggestions.title: Audit every installed SDD command for non-repository and non-Windows assumptions
suggestions.rationale: The command documents still invoke `python -m scripts.sdd.*`, `scripts/sdd/close_task.sh`, repository-relative paths, shell syntax, `jq`, and other monorepo assumptions. Moving Python helpers is insufficient unless the markdown references, hooks, and shell-only logic are rewritten or wrapped consistently. The installer should fail or report clearly when an asset references unavailable runtime tooling.

suggestions.title: Branch the global bootstrap before the existing Python guard
suggestions.rationale: The current POSIX and PowerShell installers require system Python, create a project venv with `python -m venv`, and install with pip before doing anything else. A managed mode must parse and validate its options before that guard, acquire the pinned uv binary for the platform, create/update `PARROT_HOME`, and leave project mode behavior unchanged. Add dry-run tests proving global mode works with no Python available and that partial downloads or interrupted upgrades do not leave broken shims.

suggestions.title: Gate the wheel matrix on clean install and console-script smoke tests
suggestions.rationale: The release workflow currently builds core wheels only for Linux x86_64 and Windows AMD64, while the project declares `<3.14` but the matrix includes Python 3.14. Build success alone does not prove compiler-free installation on macOS or that the launcher, MCP stdio paths, and packaged SDD assets work. Add per-platform clean-environment install/import/console-script tests and resolve the Python-version contradiction before expanding the matrix.
